title: Greenhouse temperature: average rate, Mean Value Theorem and extremes

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of H(t)H(t) over the interval 0≤t≤140 \le t \le 14. Indicate units of measure.

accept: the difference quotient with the values <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>69.771</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(14) \approx 69.771</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>62</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(0) = 62</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.555</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.555</annotation></semantics></math> (rounded or truncated; the value is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.55508</mn><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.55508\ldots</annotation></semantics></math>) with units <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi></mi><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>F per hour

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>14</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{H(14) - H(0)}{14 - 0}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>69.771</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>62</mn></mrow><mn>14</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{69.771 - 62}{14}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.555</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.555</annotation></semantics></math> degrees Fahrenheit per hour.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find H′(5)H'(5). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of H′(5)H'(5) in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.248</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H'(5) \approx -1.248</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.248</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.248</annotation></semantics></math> (rounded or truncated; the value is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.24801</mn><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.24801\ldots</annotation></semantics></math>), from a numerical derivative

rubric.point: Interpretation: at 11 a.m. (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>), the temperature in the greenhouse is decreasing at a rate of 1.248 degrees Fahrenheit per hour
accept: "changing at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.248</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.248</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi></mi><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>F per hour at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math> hours"
must name the temperature, the time and the units

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.248</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H'(5) \approx -1.248</annotation></semantics></math>. At time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math> hours (11 a.m.), the temperature in the greenhouse is decreasing at a rate of 1.248 degrees Fahrenheit per hour.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Is there a time tt, for 0<t<140 < t < 14, at which H′(t)H'(t) is equal to the average rate of change found in part (a)? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: States that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 14]</annotation></semantics></math> and differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 14)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable, so it is continuous" or "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is a sum of continuous, differentiable functions"

rubric.point: Answer yes, by the Mean Value Theorem, with the conclusion <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0.555</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H'(c) = 0.555</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 14)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: requires the hypothesis point or an equivalent statement of the hypotheses

parts.sample: Yes. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is differentiable on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 14)</annotation></semantics></math> and continuous on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 14]</annotation></semantics></math> (it is built from exponential, polynomial and sine functions). By the Mean Value Theorem, there is a time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>c</mi><mo><</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < c < 14</annotation></semantics></math> at which <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H'(c)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>14</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{H(14) - H(0)}{14}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.555</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.555</annotation></semantics></math> degrees Fahrenheit per hour.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum temperature and the absolute minimum temperature of the greenhouse for 0≤t≤140 \le t \le 14. Justify your answers.

rubric.point: Considers <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H'(t) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.864</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 3.864</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>9.747</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 9.747</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: both critical points found with the calculator

rubric.point: Candidates Test: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>62</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(0) = 62</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.864</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>72.235</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(3.864) \approx 72.235</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9.747</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>64.829</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(9.747) \approx 64.829</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>69.771</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(14) \approx 69.771</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: a table or list of the endpoints and both critical points with their values

not earned by a sign change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H'</annotation></semantics></math> alone

rubric.point: Answers: absolute maximum <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>72.235</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.235</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi></mi><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>F (at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.864</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 3.864</annotation></semantics></math>) and absolute minimum <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>62</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62</annotation></semantics></math> <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi></mi><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>F (at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: the minimum is at the endpoint <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, not at the relative minimum <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>9.747</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 9.747</annotation></semantics></math>
